title: Proper direct image preserves finite Tor amplitude
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and the standing scheme setting [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]: $k$ is a field of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, $X,Y$ are separated schemes of finite type over $k$, and $p_X:X\to Y$ is a proper $k$-morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring with $\ell^r A=0$ for some $r\ge1$. Work on the small etale sites with constant $A$-coefficients and the ordinary derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Write $\Dctf(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ for the full subcategory of $\Dbc(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes] consisting of complexes of finite Tor amplitude [def-kun-tor-amplitude].

Let $d\in\mathbf Z_{\ge0}$ be a uniform bound for the $\ell$-cohomological dimensions of the geometric fibres: for every geometric point $\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$ [def-weil-geometric-point], every $\ell$-power torsion abelian sheaf $F$ on $(X_{\bar y})_{\mathrm{et}}$, where $X_{\bar y}=X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ [def-pc-base-change] and $\ell$-power torsion means that every local section of $F$ is killed by some power of $\ell$, and every $i>d$, assume $H^i((X_{\bar y})_{\mathrm{et}},F)=0$, with etale cohomology as in [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. For integers $a\le b$ and $C\in\Dctf(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ of Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$, the total right derived direct image $Rp_{X,*}C$ belongs to $\Dctf(Y_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and has Tor amplitude in $[a,b+d]$.

proof.text: Put $K=Rp_{X,*}C$. Take $N_0=\ell^r$. The finite coefficient convention [sbc-def-coefficient-conventions] holds on $X$ and $Y$: $N_0 A=0$, and $\ell$ is a nonzero element of $k$, hence a unit, whose image stays a unit on every $k$-scheme. The morphism $p_X$ is proper between finite-type $k$-schemes, exactly the hypotheses of [lem-fin-proper-bounded-constructible]. Since $C\in\Dbc(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, that lemma gives $K\in\Dbc(Y_{\mathrm{et}},A)$.

source.place: Constructibility paragraph; Stacks Tag 0GL0 (more-etale-theorem-constructible-shriek) applies in the standing finite-type setting

proof.text:
Fix an arbitrary $A$-module $N$, with no finite generation or flatness assumption, and let $N_Y$ be its constant sheaf [def-kun-constant-sheaf]. Exactness of constant-coefficient module inverse image [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] identifies $Lp_X^*N_Y$ with the degree-zero sheaf $p_X^{-1}N_Y$. Thus $B_N=C\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}p_X^{-1}N_Y$ has cohomology only in $[a,b]$, by the definition [def-kun-tor-amplitude]. Apply [lem-etale-proper-projection-formula-finite] with $M=C$ and its second argument $N_Y[0]$. Its ring and properness hypotheses hold and it imposes no boundedness or Tor hypothesis on $N_Y$. It gives
$$K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}N_Y\simeq Rp_{X,*}B_N.$$
This is the proper projection formula (Stacks Tag 0F0G); Tag 0F12 alone states a formula for global sections and is not directly a relative pushforward theorem.

source.place: Tags 0F0G (lemma-projection-formula-proper-mod-n) and 0F12 (lemma-pull-out-constant-mod-n); realizes the first sentence of the blueprint Stalks of tensor products paragraph

proof.text:
Fix $\bar y:P=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$, let $i:X_{\bar y}\to X$ and $p_{\bar y}:X_{\bar y}\to P$ be the fibre projections. Apply [det-properbasechange-modules] to $B_N$ and this Cartesian square. The complex is bounded below by step 2 and all its cohomology sheaves are annihilated by $\ell^r$, so the required underlying torsion condition holds. It gives
$$\bar y^{-1}Rp_{X,*}B_N\simeq Rp_{\bar y,*}i^{-1}B_N.$$
By [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] and [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology], the fibre complex $E=i^{-1}B_N$ still has cohomology only in $[a,b]$. By [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-point-pullback-stalk], sections on $P_{\mathrm{et}}$ are an exact equivalence with $A$-modules, and sections of $\bar y^{-1}G$ equal $G_{\bar y}$ naturally (apply its abelian statement to the underlying sheaf and retain the action). Applying this exact functor termwise identifies the left side with $(Rp_{X,*}B_N)_{\bar y}$ and the right side with $R\Gamma(X_{\bar y},E)$: choose a bounded below K-injective representative $I$ of $E$ using [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives] and [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative]. The equality $\Gamma(P,p_{\bar y,*}I)=\Gamma(X_{\bar y},I)$ computes the right side, since the exact equivalence $\Gamma(P,-)$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms. Hence
$$(K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}N_Y)_{\bar y}\simeq R\Gamma(X_{\bar y},E).$$

source.place: Stalks of tensor products paragraph: proper base change and fibre formula; Stacks Tags 095T, 03Q1 (lemma-stalk-pullback), 04JQ (lemma-equivalence-abelian-sheaves-point)

proof.text:
Here are all hypotheses and the vanishing argument for the fibre hypercohomology sequence. The categories of $A$-module sheaves on $X_{\bar y}$ and $P$ are Grothendieck abelian by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-grothendieck-abelian]. The direct image $v=p_{\bar y,*}$ is additive and left exact by [lem-weil-pbc-module-direct-image-left-exact]. These module categories have enough injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives], and [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative] supplies a bounded below K-injective complex representing $E$, so [thm-sp-truncation-e2] applies to $v$ and that complex. Its $E_2$-page, finite exhaustive separated abutment filtrations, and the exact point-section equivalence of step 3 give
$$E_2^{s,t}=H^s(X_{\bar y},\mathcal H^t(E))\Longrightarrow H^{s+t}(X_{\bar y},E).$$
For the module-valued $H^s$ in this formula, [lem-weil-pbc-etale-module-cohomology-forget] identifies its underlying group with abelian sheaf cohomology. Each $\mathcal H^t(E)$ is killed by $\ell^r$, so the stated $\ell$-cohomological bound makes this zero for $s>d$. It is also zero for $s<0$ by the spectral sequence theorem and for $t\notin[a,b]$ by step 3. Therefore $E_2^{s,t}=0$ outside the rectangle $0\le s\le d$, $a\le t\le b$. Zero entries remain zero on later pages, since the next page is a kernel modulo an image. If $n\notin[a,b+d]$, all entries on $s+t=n$ are zero, so all associated graded objects of the finite abutment filtration of $H^n(X_{\bar y},E)$ are zero. Successively $F^j/F^{j+1}=0$ makes $F^j=F^{j+1}$; start at the zero end of the finite filtration and reach the exhaustive end. Thus $H^n(X_{\bar y},E)=0$. This proves the constant-module tensor bound at every geometric stalk without assuming constructibility of $N$ or $E$.

source.place: Tag 015J (lemma-two-ss-complex-functor), E2 page and finite convergence; realizes the final two sentences of the blueprint Stalks of tensor products paragraph

proof.text:
Let $M$ now be any sheaf of $A$-modules on $Y_{\mathrm{et}}$. At a geometric point $\bar y:P\to Y$, use [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] to identify $L\bar y^*$ with exact inverse image. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] to the ringed-topos morphism with constant coefficient rings $A_Y,A_P$; use a site skeleton small relative to the module universe [def-weil-size-convention]. Its coefficient ring map is an isomorphism by the inverse-image theorem, and its K-flat pullback clause justifies the derived tensor comparison. Under the exact equivalence of [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-point-pullback-stalk] this reads
$$(K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}M)_{\bar y}\simeq K_{\bar y}\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}M_{\bar y}.$$
The point equivalence identifies tensor products on $P$ with ordinary module tensors: both are characterized by $A$-balanced bilinear maps, The equivalence and its inverse preserve exact complexes and tensor products, hence preserve flat modules and K-flat complexes (tensoring with an acyclic complex remains acyclic under the equivalence). Applying it termwise to K-flat resolutions with flat terms therefore gives the displayed derived version. Put $N=M_{\bar y}$. The constant sheaf $N_Y$ [def-kun-constant-sheaf] has stalk $N$: every section of its sheafification is locally represented by a constant, giving surjectivity from $N$ to the stalk. If two constants have equal germs, they agree after restriction to an etale neighbourhood carrying the geometric point. Such a neighbourhood is nonempty; a covering of it has a nonempty member, and restriction in the constant presheaf does not change the element of $N$. Thus the two constants are equal, proving injectivity. Applying the same derived comparison with $N_Y$ therefore identifies the right side with $(K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}N_Y)_{\bar y}$. Steps 3-4 show that this complex has zero cohomology outside $[a,b+d]$. Exactness of the point equivalence and [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] identify these cohomology modules with the stalks of $\mathcal H^n(K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}M)$. For $n$ outside the interval the underlying abelian sheaf has zero stalks, so [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative], applied to its map to zero, makes it zero. Its module structure is then zero as well. Since $M$ was arbitrary, [def-kun-tor-amplitude] gives Tor amplitude $[a,b+d]$ for $K$. Together with step 1 and the stated definition of $\Dctf$, this proves the conclusion.

split_report.summary: Restored the explicit standing finite-type k-scheme hypotheses needed for constructibility, with a non-finite-presentation closed-immersion counterexample to the unqualified imported wording. Reused all existing DAG nodes; no new nodes. Corrected the relative use of Stacks 0F12 to the existing proper projection-formula node (0F0G), replaced the absent unit-id citation by the actual bounded-below module base-change node, verified the spectral-sequence hypotheses and finite-filtration vanishing, and supplied the derived tensor stalk justification. Recorded actual Mathlib searches and verbatim citations.
split_report.blueprint: Step 1 realizes Constructibility. Steps 2-4 realize Stalks of tensor products, with precisely the [a,b+d] bound and no finiteness condition on N. Step 5 realizes From constant modules to all sheaves. The constant-module/proper-base-change route of unit step 1 is retained.
split_report.statement_dispute: STATEMENT-DISPUTED: without the standing setting, take Y=Spec(k[t_1,t_2,...]), X=Spec(k) defined by I=(t_1,t_2,...), p the closed immersion, and A=F_ell with ell different from char(k). The constant C=A_X[0] has Tor amplitude [0,0], and every geometric fibre has ell-cohomological dimension zero. But p_*A_X has nonconstructible support {I}, since this closed point is not a constructible subset of Y (no finitely many polynomial equations cut it out). Thus the claimed Dctf conclusion fails. The corrected statement explicitly restores the chapter standing setting of sk-def-sfb-dc-setting, already required by lem-fin-proper-bounded-constructible, and writes out the etale Dctf notion for arbitrary finite commutative A. No target statement is changed.
